A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiBO research work. The full main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material that was moved or renumbered.

before.justification: V1 reports original optimization experiments on four Design-Bench tasks, component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity studies and appendix median results.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds a matched autoregressive comparison, GP-prior and sampling analyses, RNA evaluations and a pretraining-overlap probe.

M1.justification: Equation (3) revises the stated domain-adaptation loss indicator to include prompt masking alongside response masking. This is a localized loss-expression change: both versions already describe joint prompt-response reconstruction, so an implementation change is not established. The backbone, corpus construction, DA–SFT–RL pipeline and reward remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 retains the four original Design-Bench tasks and adds RNA-A/B/C from BootGen, involving length-14 RNA sequence optimization (Appendix A.6, Table 11). This substantially extends biological task coverage beyond the original DNA and robot-morphology evaluations.

E2.justification: V2 adds a matched LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct autoregressive comparator across all four original tasks and all three training stages (Table 2), providing a substantial new comparison against the diffusion backbone. The main table's named comparator set is retained. Inference-only dLLM with MCTS was excluded from quantitative comparisons in both versions; its discussion was moved.

E3.justification: V2 introduces matched-backbone controls, random versus evenly spaced pool sampling, Top-5/10/20 metrics, and ranking probes using 500 groups per task for K=2–5. It adopts dimension-scaled GP priors and changes the stated continuous-task DA learning rate from 1e-4 to 1e-5. That reported setting revision does not establish that retained experiments were rerun; newly disclosed training budgets and decoding details are documentation additions.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses testing the backbone's contribution, sensitivity to offline-pool sampling, the effect of GP priors, and possible pretrained design-label knowledge (Tables 2, 6, 8 and 12). These address important questions absent from v1. The delimiter, training-stage, context-similarity and hyperparameter analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify eight random seeds and mean ± standard deviation for optimization results. V2 introduces no new confidence intervals, significance tests or changed repeated-run counts. Additional result rows and the ranking probe's sample size do not establish a change in uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: DiBO's four headline maximum scores remain unchanged, but GP results and rankings change under revised priors; for example, Grad-EI's TF Bind 8 maximum changes from 0.673 to 0.864. DiBO's TF Bind 8 median changes from 0.599 in v1 Table 5 to 0.473 in v2 Tables 9–10, although v2 Table 8 retains 0.599. Numerous new results include mixed RNA outcomes: DiBO leads maximum scores on RNA-A/C but trails both comparators on every reported RNA-B metric.

T1.justification: Equation (3) adds a prompt-mask condition to the formal loss indicator, changing its mathematical expression rather than merely its typography. The other training objectives and similarity definition are retained, and neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: adapting diffusion LLMs through a unified delimiter-based corpus and domain adaptation, followed by SFT and RL, achieves strong small-data BBO performance. The added experiments support these existing claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 broadens interpretation through the matched-backbone results, GP-prior sensitivity, mixed RNA findings and pretraining-knowledge audit. It explicitly acknowledges that unavailable pretraining data prevent an exact overlap audit. Section 4.6 also narrows the earlier interpretation about avoiding 'prompt hacking' to robustness under natural paraphrases that preserve task semantics and output format.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents stage-specific optimization steps and processed sample counts, inference-context resampling, single-pass greedy token filling, and duplicate rejection until 128 unique valid candidates are obtained. It adds representative paraphrases, GP implementation information and the ranking-probe procedure. The abstract's code hyperlink changes from an anonymous repository to the named DiBO GitHub repository; these are documented access instructions, not independently verified availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds literature supporting high-dimensional GP calibration and implementation, including Hvarfner, Binois and Wycoff, Garnett and BoTorch, plus BootGen and additional BBO/multimodal citations. The central positioning relative to autoregressive optimization and inference-only diffusion remains intact. Publication updates for existing works and removal of a duplicate ICT reference do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: The main section order and most existing prose remain intact. V2 makes targeted wording changes, expands implementation and appendix explanations, rewrites the prompt-robustness discussion and conclusion, and moves the inference-only comparison into Section 4.4. Author/affiliation and proceedings-header text also change; there is no wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 adds substantial displays for the matched backbone comparison, pool sampling, prompt paraphrases, GP-prior comparisons, Top-K performance, RNA results and ranking audit. Existing ablation tables are regrouped and renumbered, and Figure 2 is relocated with a shorter caption. The two existing figures retain essentially the same visual content.

improvement.justification: The matched trained autoregressive control and calibrated GP comparisons substantially strengthen evidence for DiBO's advantages beyond v1's comparisons. Explicit training budgets and inference procedures resolve important reproducibility gaps, while RNA evaluations and a narrower paraphrase interpretation better expose applicability boundaries. These gains outweigh a material reporting defect: v2 gives conflicting TF Bind 8 medians, 0.599 in Table 8 versus 0.473 in Tables 9–10. The improvement concerns stronger evaluation and documentation, not increased headline DiBO scores.
